title: Introduce epochal-gap-runner with SLA-aware backpressure and per-cohort coverage exporter
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a new workload runner (epochal-gap-runner) that generates phased requests with controlled gaps and exposes per-cohort coverage metrics; useful for reproducing SLA regressions and cold-start amplification scenarios.
body:
Motivation: Reproduce and profile a class of production regressions where brief, regularly spaced 'epoch gaps' (periods of very low traffic) amplify cold-start sensitivity and cause p95/p99 volatility when combined with heterogeneous cohort priming. Existing runners focus on bursty or steady-state mixes; we needed a compact runner that generates deterministic epoch boundaries, injects controlled inter-epoch gaps, and triggers an SLA-aware backpressure policy in the serving runtime so we can measure both latency amplification and fairness across cohorts.

What this PR does: Adds epochal-gap-runner and a companion coverage exporter. The runner supports: (1) epoch windows with configurable active/gap durations and jitter, (2) per-cohort priming sequences that can be pinned to different models/quantization profiles, (3) a feedback hook that simulates client-side backpressure based on observed tail latency (SLA thresholds), and (4) deterministic trace anchors to map requests to epoch boundaries in telemetry. The coverage exporter aggregates token-path coverage per cohort and emits a compact histogram + sparse sample set for downstream differential analysis.

Design notes: The runner operates in three phases per epoch: warmup (primer requests), steady (target qps), and gap (near-zero QPS). We intentionally introduce a small randomized skew across cohorts to model non-synchronous priming observed in multi-tenant deployments. The SLA-aware backpressure module is conservative: when simulated p99 exceeds threshold, it reduces offered load for cohorts proportionally to recent amplification factor and emits a backpressure event. This allows testing of runtime admission policies and fairness strategies without modifying production traffic generators.

Checklist: [x] new runner implementation; [x] unit tests for epoch alignment and backpressure heuristics; [x] end-to-end integration test against local perf-canary harness; [x] telemetry exporter + example dashboard config; [x] docs snippet in benchmark-lab/README describing knobs and usage.

Commits summary: commit 1: add epochal-gap-runner core, CLI and config schema; commit 2: implement SLA backpressure feedback and cohort skewing; commit 3: add coverage exporter and histogram encoder; commit 4: unit and integration tests; commit 5: docs + examples; commit 6: fix race in shutdown path (review feedback).

Files changed (high-level): ["benchmark-lab/runners/epochal_gap_runner.py", "benchmark-lab/telemetry/coverage_exporter.go", "benchmark-lab/tests/test_epochal_gap.py", "benchmark-lab/examples/epochal_gap_example.yaml", "benchmark-lab/docs/epochal_gap_runner.md", "benchmark-lab/Cargo.toml" (minor), "benchmark-lab/ci/workflow-bench.yml", "benchmark-lab/internal/backpressure/strategy.rs"].

Small illustrative snippet (runner config example):
```
epochs: 60
active_ms: 45000
gap_ms: 15000
cohorts:
  - name: web-1
    primer_tokens: 64
    target_qps: 35
  - name: mobile-2
    primer_tokens: 16
    target_qps: 80
sla:
  p99_threshold_ms: 220
  slowdown_factor: 0.5
```

Testing and telemetry: Unit tests cover epoch boundary detection, backpressure triggers, and coverage exporter serialization. Integration run on the perf-canary infra produced stable reproduction of the incident profile in ~3 runs. The coverage exporter emits a compact per-cohort token-path histogram and a sparse set of representative prompt ids; we validated ingestion into the latency-analyzer pipeline and added a candidate view in Grafana (dashboard JSON in examples).

Review conversation (high level): Reviewer Marco Nguyen requested tightening of the shutdown/race path for the backpressure goroutine — addressed in commit 6 by switching to a bounded channel and explicit cancel token. Elena asked for clearer nomenclature between 'gap' and 'cooldown' and suggested adding a jitter knob; renamed config fields and added max_gap_jitter_ms. Zachary requested limits on coverage exporter memory growth for very large vocab traces — implemented streaming encoder with periodic flush. All reviewers approved after the fixes.

CI: Initial CI run failed due to a flaky test in test_epochal_gap related to system clock mocking. Flaky test was hardened (use monotonic clock) and CI was re-run; all checks passed on rerun. See 'ci_checks' field for details.

Rollout: Merged to main and marked non-breaking. We will schedule a canary run on the staging perf cluster and run a short 2-hour sweep with 3 cohort permutations to collect baseline coverage and SLA amplification curves. Follow-up work (ENG-1401) will add a controller to automatically sweep different primer token sizes for model/quantization sensitivity scanning.
commits_summary: add epochal-gap-runner CLI + core; add SLA backpressure feedback; coverage exporter with histogram encoder; unit/integration tests; docs and examples; fix shutdown race (final)
review_comments: Marco: race in backpressure goroutine, use bounded channel or cancel token — fixed in commit 6
Elena: rename 'cooldown' to 'gap' and add jitter knob — config renamed and max_gap_jitter_ms added
Zachary: coverage exporter memory growth — switched to streaming encoder with periodic flush; added integration test to validate memory usage
notes_for_maintainers: This runner intentionally generates deterministic epoch boundaries; when instrumenting the runtime please keep the trace anchors stable across releases (see docs for trace anchor format). The coverage exporter protocol is intentionally compact — adding fields will require bumping the encoder version string.
